Name: Apache Spark
Use Case: Batch ETL, ML training, ad-hoc analytics
Weaknesses: Heavy JVM cluster, slower than Flink for true streaming
Notes: Use Spark for batch / lakehouse ETL; reach for Flink when low-latency streaming dominates.

Name: Apache Flink
Strengths: Best-in-class event-time semantics, stateful streaming, exactly-once
Weaknesses: Smaller community than Spark, ops complexity
Tooling: Flink Kubernetes Operator, Ververica, Confluent Cloud
Keywords: flink streaming event time stateful exactly once
Notes: Pair with Kafka + RocksDB state backend; use 'savepoints' for upgrades.

Name: Kafka Streams / ksqlDB
Strengths: No extra cluster (runs inside your JVM app), exactly-once with Kafka tx
Weaknesses: JVM-only; Kafka-coupled; harder for huge state
Notes: Excellent for stream-processing close to a Kafka source without standing up Flink/Spark.

Name: Airbyte / Fivetran / Stitch / Meltano
Strengths: Hundreds of connectors, managed schema evolution
Weaknesses: SaaS cost; vendor connector quality varies
Notes: Use 'dlt' (open source, Python) for code-first pipelines; Airbyte/Fivetran for click-driven.

Name: dbt
Strengths: SQL + Jinja, tests, docs, lineage; hugely popular
Weaknesses: Limited orchestration (use Airflow/Dagster); dbt Core vs Cloud features differ
Keywords: dbt jinja sql transform model lineage
Notes: Standard for modern T in EL-T. Pair with Airflow/Dagster for orchestration.

Name: Apache Airflow
Weaknesses: Operationally heavy, dynamic DAGs are awkward
Notes: Airflow 2.x is much better but consider Dagster/Prefect for new projects.

Name: Dagster
Use Case: Data assets with lineage, materialisations, type checks
Strengths: Asset graph + observability; tighter dev-loop than Airflow
Notes: Asset-first model fits modern lakehouse / dbt stacks naturally.

Name: Prefect
Notes: Lightweight Pythonic alternative; great for ML pipelines.

Name: Iceberg / Delta Lake / Hudi
Use Case: ACID + schema evolution + time-travel on object storage
Tooling: Iceberg + Athena / Snowflake / BigQuery; Delta + Databricks; Hudi + EMR
Notes: Iceberg has the strongest cross-engine momentum (AWS, Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks all support reads/writes).

Name: ClickHouse / Druid / Pinot
Use Case: Real-time analytics on streams (product analytics, ad-tech)
Strengths: Sub-second on huge data; real-time ingest
Notes: ClickHouse is the simplest single-binary; Druid/Pinot for high-cardinality real-time aggregations.

Name: Spark Structured Streaming + Delta
Strengths: Same engine for batch & streaming; ACID via Delta
Notes: Pragmatic 'one engine' choice if Spark already exists in stack.

Name: Debezium
Use Case: Change data capture from RDBMS into Kafka
Strengths: Low-impact log-based CDC for Postgres/MySQL/Mongo/SQL Server
Keywords: debezium cdc binlog wal kafka connect
Notes: Pair with Iceberg/Delta sink for streaming-to-lakehouse pipelines.

Name: Kafka Connect
Use Case: Move data into/out of Kafka without writing code
Notes: Use distributed mode + offsets in Kafka topics; monitor connector lag.

Name: LakeFS / Nessie
Use Case: Branch / merge / rollback your data lake
Keywords: lakefs nessie data versioning git for data
Notes: Useful for ML reproducibility and lakehouse migrations.

Name: Vector DBs (Qdrant/Milvus/Weaviate/Pinecone/pgvector)
Notes: Start with pgvector; switch to dedicated vector DB once QPS / recall demand it.

Name: Feature stores (Feast / Tecton / Hopsworks)
Notes: Adopt only when multiple models share features and online/offline parity matters.
